# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This Quarto book serves as a user tutorial for the `fdid` package in R, which implements the **Factorial Difference-in-Differences (FDID)** framework introduced by @xu2026factorial\[<a href="https://yiqingxu.org/papers/2025_fdid/fdid.pdf" target="_blank">Paper</a>\]. This design is tailored for panel data settings where all units are exposed to a universal event but vary in a baseline factor $G$, which can be binary or continuous depending on the estimator.

`fdid` provides four main user-facing functions:

-   `fdid_prepare()`: reshapes long format panel data into a wide `fdid()`-ready format.
-   `fdid()`: performs factorial difference-in-differences estimation using several methods.
-   `fdid_contrast()`: reports continuous-$G$ level contrasts from fitted curve objects.
-   `fdid_derivative()`: reports fixed-$G$ derivative values from fitted curve objects.

And two S3 methods:

-   `summary()`: summarizes the estimation results.
-   `plot()`: visualizes raw means, dynamic effects, continuous-$G$ curves, and model comparisons.

## Organization

The user tutorial is structured into the following chapters:

-   [Chapter @sec-start]\
    Installation instructions and dataset description.

-   [Chapter @sec-binary]\
    Data preparation, estimation with binary $G$, and basic plots.

-   [Chapter @sec-continuous]\
    Estimation with continuous $G$ using linear, kernel, and DML methods,
    including a roadmap for level curves, level contrasts, and derivative
    estimands.

-   [Chapter @sec-kernel-continuous]\
    A focused kernel-estimator workflow: support diagnostics, estimation-grid
    choices, pointwise versus bootstrap curve bands, and reporting helpers.

-   [Chapter @sec-dml-continuous]\
    A focused DML workflow: target mapping, scalar PLR, flexible DML curves,
    incremental average derivatives, inference labels, and sensitivity checks.

-   [Chapter @sec-visualization]\
    Extended visualization options, continuous-$G$ level and derivative curves,
    and method comparisons.

-   [Chapter @sec-sensitivity]\
    Sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding using `sensemakr`.

## Report bugs

Please report any bugs to me (yiqingxu \[at\] stanford.edu) or submit an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/xuyiqing/fdid/issues). Please include your minimally replicable code and data files and a **panelView** treatment status plot. Your feedback is highly valued!
